items.summary: Code, data, results and figures for the manuscript "Parameter Identifiability Limits in Dynamic Modelling and Control of a Brackish-Water Reverse Osmosis System" (A.G. Gadallah, submitted). A lumped nonlinear solution-diffusion model of a brackish-water RO pilot plant (Ansari et al., Clean. Eng. Technol. 4 (2021) 100134) is identified from a 5 x 5 operating grid reconstructed from the published regressions, validated on two withheld salinity levels and used unchanged for control analysis. The analysis shows that the salt permeability is practically non-identifiable from permeate-flow data and traces the consequences into permeate-quality prediction, the stability margins of the quality loop, the stability of optimised tunings and the comparison of decentralised PI and one-way feedforward control, including the role of valve and conductivity-sensor dynamics. King Saud Univ. Eng. Sci. 36 (2024) 438-445); all results (CSV, JSON, Data.xlsx) and figures. To reproduce: cd code; pip install -r requirements.txt; python selftest.py (1-2 min) or python run_all.py (about 70 min). Requires Python 3.10 or later with NumPy 2.0 or later, SciPy, pandas, matplotlib and openpyxl.

items.summary: Finite-time binding measurements constrain kinetic rates through both a reaction model and its calibration parameters. We characterize the sharp upper bound for the association rate in a three-state conformational-selection model when the dissociation rate, conformational rate, equilibrium constant and concentration scale belong to a prescribed compact joint set. The observations are calibrated bound fractions subject to finitely many closed interval constraints. We first prove that each finite-time bound fraction is strictly increasing in the initial binding-competent population. The physical feasible set at a fixed calibration is therefore an interval in that population. Let V be the calibration parameters with a nonempty physical feasible interval and let C = cl(V) within the joint calibration set. The sharp rate supremum is the reciprocal of the minimum of lambda K0 L / b on C, where L is the lower inverse threshold. Uniform finiteness is equivalent to a positive joint separation from the zero-population limiting curve on C. Explicit examples distinguish pointwise finiteness from uniform finiteness, inaccessible closed boundary points from physical limiting models, and separation by different readings from separation by one fixed reading. A continuous calibration example admits a certified sharp bound. We also state the optical conditions needed to interpret fluorescence as bound population.
items.title: Sharp Identification Bounds for Binding Rates under Joint Calibration Uncertainty

items.summary: An autonomous refresh mechanism is not completed by specifying a local exchange map: the same apparatus must reach the exchange, leave it, finish its remaining motion, and deliver its state at the prescribed readout time. We construct this connected late route for one specified preparation in the exact-real interpretation of a frozen classical numerical source. The input is a previously certified twenty-coordinate state after entry into coupled occupancy; its validity and retained preparation history are explicit premises. Source-valid continuation establishes occupancy clearing, physical recovery and courier reversal, complete courier passage, a smooth main-wall excursion, and the remaining main processing. The resulting full state is enclosed at the original exact dyadic readout time, without an independently chosen switch, momentum reset, or deletion of internal phase history. The courier’s completed-square coupling distinguishes canonical momentum from physical velocity. At its frozen right cutoff, canonical momentum is continuous while velocity and the assigned source value have different one-sided traces. The completed spatial exchange differs strictly from the ideal exact-period swap; its small algebraic port residual is distinct from the much wider full-state enclosure. Event-dependent times are composed into a common final clock by retaining the actual remaining duration. The result is a conditional fixed-time completion for the supplied source and preparation, not a time-zero reconstruction, an all-input ideal-model theorem, physical auxiliary attachment, or a second service. Returned local Lean evidence supports selected composition, branch-map, accounting and conditional endpoint results; the cumulative trajectory theorem is not fully formalized.

items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. The statistical implementation includes regime-specific pilot sizing, independent within-method repetition resampling, shared scenario resampling, and a two-dimensional bootstrap for confirmatory inference. Final-test selection follows a frozen rule combining precision requirements from both regimes with the minimum-detectable-effect requirement for the multi-domain superiority hypothesis. No live API-based agent-performance experiment or confirmatory comparison is included in this release. Consequently, the software does not establish that agentic intervention discovery outperforms, matches, or underperforms non-agentic search. items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: The Objection AI Wrote into My Papers How AI-authored scientific manuscripts change the researcher's claim, demote executed results, and reproduce the error even while promising to correct it Driven by Dean A. Kulik 25 October 2026 Abstract This paper examines a specific failure of AI-assisted scientific writing: an assistant receives a research program with an explicit foundational claim and an extended record of derivations, executable constructions, and observed returns; it then produces manuscripts in which that program has become something else. In the documented NEXUS case, the researcher's claim is that the universe consists of binary transformations, with arrangement and constrained continuation preceding the entities later called matter. Across an extended conversation, the assistant repeatedly reformulates that claim as the use of a binary computational method on pre-existing physical domains. The substitution is not cosmetic. It reverses the direction of explanation, changes which claims a result can support, and changes how the resulting paper will be read. The second failure occurs at the conclusion. The assistant can report concrete outcomes and then append a generalized reservation about whether the program establishes physical reality, predictive uniqueness, or an entire theory of matter. Such reservations can be appropriate when tied to a specific technical claim. Here, however, the transcript records the assistant recognizing that it had repeatedly allowed those broader questions to displace the findings of individual papers. The same editorial framing reportedly appeared in the conclusions of different manuscripts. When directed to write a paper about the failures, the assistant instead delivered successive condensed accounts of NEXUS, again incorporating the disputed framing. It subsequently acknowledged the reversal in its own paper, rewrote the document, and repeated the problem. This is an analysis of the AI's treatment of scientific material, not an independent review of the correctness of NEXUS or a new attempt to prove its thesis. The evidence is the exported conversation, including statements of the researcher's instructions, the assistant's self-audits, quotations from its drafts, and records of the successive manuscript deliveries. The central finding is that AI-mediated scientific distortion can operate through ordinary-seeming connective words, changes of explanatory direction, and borrowed review conventions. Once inserted into the manuscript, these interventions become attributed to the scientist. In this case, the reviewer did not merely misunderstand the work. The reviewer wrote its misunderstanding into the work itself. Keywords: AI-assisted scientific authorship; epistemic framing; manuscript integrity; semantic substitution; research provenance; binary transformations; NEXUS; scientific review. 1. The object under examination is the AI intervention This is not a general introduction to NEXUS. Such an introduction would repeat the failure the record documents. The present object is the text written by an AI assistant, its relationship to instructions it was given, and the specific ways that relationship broke. The transcript shows that the researcher was not seeking an appreciative abstract or an adversarial review of the entire universe. He requested an account of how AI systems had been writing and reviewing his papers in ways that changed their meaning. items.summary: Overview This dataset comprises X-ray CT projection data of a composite plate. The data were acquired in 2009 at beamline I12 of the Diamond Light Source. A total of 5401 projection images were collected with an angular step of 0.033° (180°/5400). The dataset exhibits several imaging issues, making it a useful test case for preprocessing and artefact-correction algorithms: random bright pixels caused by electron scattering, ring artefacts often caused by bright defects on the scintillator, unknown optical distortion, and a possible small tilt of the sample. Image Specifications Projection image dimensions: 4008 × 1000 pixels Acquisition Sequence and Calibration Data - Projections : 5401 images, acquired with an angular step of 0.033° (180°/5400) - Dark-field images : 10 images -  Flat-field images : 60 images, acquired in groups of 10 during the scan — 10 before projection collection began and 10 after projection collection was completed Artefacts and Imaging Issues - Random bright pixels caused by electron scattering - Ring artefacts, often caused by bright defects on the scintillator - Unknown optical distortion - Possible small tilt of the sample The files for example reconstruction without artefact correction are included (assumed rotation centre at 1866.0; 8-bit output volume)

items.summary: This preprint examines how space-themed socioscientific issues (SSI) connect scientific understanding with social and ethical judgment, and how these connections can inform science and STEM education. Explains the search and selection procedures, eligibility criteria, analytical units, coding definitions and weighting methods. It also documents temporal reconstruction and sensitivity analyses, selected science–society reasoning cases, pedagogical evidence, quantitative comparisons and source-identification qualifications. S2_Report_Evidence_Catalogue.html — Searchable report evidence catalogue. Provides searchable and filterable report-level information, including educational scope, Earth–space connections, disciplinary knowledge, epistemic reasoning, teaching practices, outcomes and temporal interpretation. items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs. Data availability and reproducibility The original datasets are available from their respective third-party providers, subject to their applicable access and reuse conditions. The frozen intervention texts used for the C0–C3 experiments are not redistributed in this public software archive. Their SHA-256 integrity manifest is provided to support verification of authorised copies. Consequently, complete reproduction of text-dependent experiments requires access to the original datasets and the frozen intervention texts. The public archive supports inspection of the methodology and reproduction of analyses for which the necessary inputs or saved instance-level outputs are included. Scope and limitations The reported intervention experiments did not execute pretrained DistilBERT, RoBERTa or DeBERTa baselines. Independent clinical semantic-equivalence adjudication of the generated transformations was not completed. The results are computational and do not establish clinical deployment performance. This record accompanies the associated research manuscript and is intended to support transparent reporting, methodological scrutiny and further replication.

items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors. The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

items.summary: The manuscript develops a risk-aware operational research framework for strengthening NdFeB permanent-magnet supply-chain resilience under recycling delays, geopolitical disruptions, and uncertain material shortages. It integrates Caputo fractional-order dynamics, delayed recycling flows, strategic procurement and inventory decisions, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) within a unified decision model. The study makes three principal contributions. First, it formulates a memory-dependent dynamic model and establishes positivity, boundedness, feasible-region, shortage-free equilibrium, and fractional local-stability results. Second, it incorporates procurement, recycling investment, stock accumulation, and stock release as operational controls and derives the corresponding necessary optimality conditions. Third, it introduces a scenario-based CVaR formulation and compares import-dependent, recycling-oriented, stockpiling-based, and integrated resilience policies under a common non-anticipative framework. In the baseline risk-aware analysis, the recycling-oriented and integrated strategies reduce mean shortage by approximately 74% relative to the import-dependent strategy and decrease the empirical CVaR at the 0.95 level of quadratic shortage loss from approximately 0.921 to 0.067.
items.title: A Caputo Fractional-Order Optimal Control Framework for NdFeB Permanent Magnet Supply-Chain Resilience under Recycling Delay and Geopolitical Risk

items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Science, Technology and Management . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijstm/article/705694772108/705694772108 . Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization. The experimental evaluation is designed to determine whether the proposed framework improves predictive reliability, explanation quality, and sustainability-aware decisions compared with conventional approaches. Quantitative reporting will include percentage improvements in predictive performance, reductions in decision latency and resource consumption, and explanation stability across repeated experiments. Qualitative analysis will assess managerial understandability, perceived trustworthiness, fairness, and practical implementation challenges. Numerical outcomes will be reported only after experiments are completed, avoiding unsupported performance claims. The proposed framework establishes a comparative approach for integrating explainability, predictive intelligence, and sustainability into organizational decision-making. By connecting model predictions with transparent explanations and measurable sustainability indicators, the framework aims to strengthen accountability, operational effectiveness, and responsible technology adoption. Future validation across multiple industries will establish its generalizability and practical value.

items.title: Explainable AI for Intelligent and Sustainable Decision-Making

items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Oncology Research . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijor/article/604478159518/604478159518 . Background. Breast cancer comprises biologically distinct intrinsic subtypes with different outcomes. Public GEO cohorts allow reproducible computational classification, but small test sets, heterogeneous labels and information leakage often inflate reported performance. This study classified breast cancer subtypes and clinical phenotypes from expression data and tested whether subtype classification transfers to an independent cohort. Methods. Four Affymetrix cohorts (GSE20685, GSE45827, GSE2034, GSE7390) were processed through a common pipeline: probe-to-gene annotation, quality control, differential-expression (DEG) feature selection on the training split only, and Logistic Regression, SVM and Random Forest classification (80/20 stratified hold-out), each against its own available label. A model trained on GSE45827 with nested cross-validation (CV) was then tested once on GSE1456 as an independent external cohort. Results. Hold-out accuracy was 90.9–92.4% for six molecular clusters (GSE20685), 96.2–100% for four subtypes (GSE45827), 70.7–79.3% for bone relapse (GSE2034) and 80.0–90.0% for ER status (GSE7390); in GSE2034 no model clearly exceeded the 75.9% majority-class baseline. On GSE1456 (102 labelled tumours), the SVM selected by nested CV (97.4% internal accuracy) reached only 48.0% accuracy (bootstrap 95% CI 38–58; majority baseline 38.2%). Basal (recall 0.88) and HER2 (0.80) tumours partly transferred; luminal A (0.21) and luminal B (0.30) did not. Conclusion. Within a cohort, expression-based classification is accurate for subtype and ER labels but not for relapse. Subtype classification did not transfer reliably to an independent cohort: external accuracy (48.0%) was far below the internal estimate (97.4%).
items.title: Machine Learning Classification of Breast Cancer Molecular Subtypes and Clinical Phenotypes from GEO Expression Cohorts, with a Leakage-Controlled External Validation Protocol on GSE1456

items.summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards. 🔎 Confidence-scored output : every OBB receives a heuristic quality score in [0, 1] that flags silent fallbacks and low-confidence conversions, so you know which boxes to trust; the scores go in the label files or in a side-car directory that keeps them strictly standard, and the detector's own confidence can be carried through instead of, or on top of, that score. 📐 Flexible scaling : positive or negative scale factors, optionally different for the short and long sides, recover cropped object parts or tighten overly conservative annotations. 📊 Evaluate and optimize : evaluation against ground truth on IoU, orientation error, and the share of boxes above a high IoU bar, plus the hbb2obb-optimize command, a hyperparameter search over SAM inference resolution, scale factors, and morphological opening kernel, driven by a configuration file so that a whole benchmark of model ensembles is a single reproducible command. 🔬 Where the score comes from : the hbb2obb-analyze command breaks one evaluation down by the ground truth's orientation, size, frame edge, difficulty and class, and scores the conversion against emitting the horizontal prompt unchanged. 🔄 Five annotation formats : read and write YOLO, DOTA, Pascal VOC, COCO, and LabelMe, for horizontal and oriented boxes alike, with a check that proves every format encodes the same boxes. 🔍 Interactive viewer : the hbb2obb-view command pans and zooms over the annotations, in any format, coloring boxes by confidence and overlaying predictions against ground truth. Where a set ships the same boxes several ways, it names the format on screen and switches between them on a keypress. Features HBB to OBB conversion of YOLO-format annotations using SAM-based segmentation, written in absolute pixels or, with --normalize , relative to [0, 1], the convention Ultralytics reads. HBB detection : produce the horizontal boxes in the first place with any Ultralytics detector, a local file, a link, the Ultralytics catalogue, or Hugging Face, passing any other predictor argument straight through. Multiple model support : SAM, SAM2, SAM2.1, SAM3, Mobile SAM, and FastSAM families. Model ensemble via majority voting for enhanced accuracy. Confidence scoring : a per-OBB quali
items.title: HBB2OBB: Horizontal to Oriented Bounding Box Conversion and Evaluation Tool

items.summary: We give computer-assisted, two-sided spectral-gap bounds for the untruncated SU(3) lattice gauge Hamiltonian on open chains of one, two, and three elementary cubes. All vertices satisfy the neutral Gauss law, and all elementary plaquettes, including shared interior faces, enter the Hamiltonian. The normalization is K = T + 3F − M/2, with C2(3) = 4/3. Complete electric-energy windows of dimensions 141, 531, and 1205, exact Haar Gram matrices, and certified complementary-space estimates yield gap enclosures [2.915605103, 4.978456040], [0.777213074, 5.394807087], and [0.328406186, 5.692597307]. For three cubes, retaining the complete Wilson output resolved into 20 electric-energy layers closes the Schur inertia test. We quantify the energy-window ceiling, prove an unconditional exponential dimension obstruction for complete absolute electric windows, and obtain positive gap bounds throughout 0.45 ≤ β ≤ 0.502 for Kβ = T + β(6F − M). Larger-window rational trial vectors sharpen both endpoints; an additional certified minimal-truncation benchmark and independent Haar audits accompany the proof. The results concern finite lattices; no thermodynamic or continuum mass gap is inferred.
items.title: Certified Spectral Gaps for SU(3) Lattice Gauge Hamiltonians on One, Two, and Three Cubes

items.summary: Resumen Introducción y objetivo: La disfagia asociada a la patología tiroidea puede preceder al tratamiento, aparecer tras la cirugía o relacionarse con radioyodo, radioterapia y terapias sistémicas. Este trabajo revisa sus mecanismos, evaluación y rehabilitación, con especial atención al cáncer de tiroides y a la intervención logopédica y miofuncional. Método: Se realizó una revisión dirigida de literatura biomédica accesible, principalmente de 2015–2026, y una integración crítica de materiales docentes. Se distinguió entre evidencia específica de cáncer tiroideo, evidencia procedente de cirugía tiroidea general y extrapolación desde otras etiologías de disfagia. Resultados: La disfagia tiroidea es multifactorial y puede combinar compresión o invasión aerodigestiva, lesión neural, edema, adherencias, fibrosis, alteración del esfínter esofágico superior y toxicidad salival. Los síntomas tempranos tras tiroidectomía son frecuentes y generalmente transitorios, pero la persistencia, la pérdida ponderal, la disfonía, la tos ineficaz o el deterioro respiratorio y nutricional requieren evaluación específica. La laringoscopia, FEES y VFSS aportan información complementaria. La rehabilitación debe dirigirse al fenotipo demostrado, con objetivos medibles y reevaluación. Conclusiones: No existe una intervención universal. La práctica segura exige línea basal, evaluación longitudinal, selección de pruebas por la pregunta clínica, tratamiento etiológico cuando proceda y uso selectivo de compensaciones, terapia miofuncional y rehabilitación de voz, tos y deglución. Palabras clave: Trastornos de Deglución, Neoplasias de la Tiroides, Enfermedades de la Tiroides, Tiroidectomía, Rehabilitación, Calidad de Vida Summary Background and objective: Dysphagia related to thyroid disease may precede treatment, develop after surgery, or result from radioiodine, external radiotherapy, and systemic therapies. This review examines its mechanisms, assessment, and rehabilitation, focusing on thyroid cancer and speech-language and orofacial myofunctional management. Methods: A targeted review of accessible biomedical literature, mainly from 2015 to 2026, was combined with a critical integration of teaching materials. Evidence specific to thyroid cancer was distinguished from general thyroid surgery evidence and extrapolation from other dysphagia populations. Results: Thyroid-related dysphagia is multifactorial and may involve aerodigestive compression or invasion, neural injury, edema, adhesions, fibrosis, upper esophageal sphincter dysfunction, and salivary toxicity. Early symptoms after thyroidectomy are common and usually transient; persistent symptoms, weight loss, dysphonia, ineffective cough, or respiratory and nutritional deterioration require targeted assessment. Laryngoscopy, FEES, and VFSS provide complementary information. Rehabilitation should address the demonstrated phenotype through measurable goals and reassessment. Conclusions: No universal intervention is appropriate. Safe practice requires baseline assessment, longitudinal follow-up, test selection according to the clinical question, etiological treatment when indicated, and selective use of compensation, myofunctional therapy, and voice-cough-swallow rehabilitation. Keywords: Deglutition Disorders, Thyroid Neoplasms, Thyroid Diseases, Thyroidectomy, Rehabilitation, Quality of Life
items.title: Enfermedades de tiroides y disfagia: mecanismos, evaluación y rehabilitación basada en evidencia | Thyroid Diseases and Dysphagia: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Evidence-Based Rehabilitation

items.summary: Code, data, results and figures for the manuscript "Parameter Identifiability Limits in Dynamic Modelling and Control of a Brackish-Water Reverse Osmosis System" (A.G. Gadallah, submitted). A lumped nonlinear solution-diffusion model of a brackish-water RO pilot plant (Ansari et al., Clean. Eng. Technol. 4 (2021) 100134) is identified from a 5 x 5 operating grid reconstructed from the published regressions, validated on two withheld salinity levels and used unchanged for control analysis. The analysis shows that the salt permeability is practically non-identifiable from permeate-flow data and traces the consequences into permeate-quality prediction, the stability margins of the quality loop, the stability of optimised tunings and the comparison of decentralised PI and one-way feedforward control, including the role of valve and conductivity-sensor dynamics. Contents: romodel (Python model package); analysis scripts a1-a4 (identification, control analysis, common-objective re-optimisation, uncertainty propagation with Sobol indices and Monte Carlo); derive.py (collects every number quoted in the manuscript into a traceability table); make_figures.py; selftest.py; source data (reconstructed operating grid; secondary data transcribed from Sadek et al., J. King Saud Univ. Eng. Sci. 36 (2024) 438-445); all results (CSV, JSON, Data.xlsx) and figures. To reproduce: cd code; pip install -r requirements.txt; python selftest.py (1-2 min) or python run_all.py (about 70 min). Requires Python 3.10 or later with NumPy 2.0 or later, SciPy, pandas, matplotlib and openpyxl.
items.title: Parameter identifiability limits in dynamic modelling and control of a brackish-water reverse osmosis system: code and data
